title: Adaptive Model Arbitration for Locale‑Aware Pairwise Scoring
creator: Amira Patel
description: Build an arbitration layer that dynamically selects between high-quality pairwise scorers (dense cross-attention variants) and lightweight locale-optimized scorers at request time. Goal is to improve end-to-end relevance for high-risk locales while keeping average p95 latency under 450ms and cost growth <10% for production rerank traffic.
impact_summary: Expected to raise MRR@10 for low-resource locales by 8-12% while reducing latency regressions during peak by routing cost-sensitive requests to quantized fallbacks. Will enable conservative rollout of new pairwise model variants with per-locale acceptance gates.
success_criteria: Offline: new arbitration improves per-locale MRR@10 over baseline for >=75% of locales sampled
Perf: p50/p95 latency for rerank endpoint remains <= 250ms / 450ms on global 95th percentile
Cost: serving cost delta <= +10% (token compute) compared to current fleet
Safety: no significant negative quality regression in top-10 snippets for top-3 customers during 2-week canary
technical_work: Add arbitration policy in inference graph: rules = {locale table, request type, SLAs, error budget, current capacity signal}
Implement lightweight locale-specific scorer: 6-bit quantized single-pass encoder with pairwise classifier head
Integrate cross-attention high-quality scorer variants as optional targets with KV cache warmstart support
Expose per-request model_hint and route override in API and Console for canary control
Metrics: add per-route MRR@k, MAP@k, p50/p95 latency, qps, cost-per-req to Console and eval dashboard
Regression gates: automated checks comparing shadowed outputs using tie-break thresholds and significance test (A/B bootstrap)
Operational: add autoscaling policy hook to prefer low-cost scorer when cluster GPU headroom < 12%
experiments_and_results: Offline AB: sample 200k queries (12 locales) — locales with training-data sparsity saw +9.1% MRR@10 using locale-aware scorer vs baseline cross-attention
Latency sim: instrumented p95 for heavy scorer = 620ms (single-GPU, small batch); lightweight scorer p95 = 180ms
Cost sim: fully converted 6-bit scorer reduces per-token GPU cycles by ~38% in simulation
Shadow canary (internal): 1% traffic for 3 days — correlation drift detected in locale 'pt-BR' (stat sig, p=0.02), triggered manual rollback and model hyperparam tune
Resulting action: raised locale-specific training weight and added conservative threshold for automatic promotion
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Lab — finalize model artifacts & KV-warmstart integration (1 week)
Stage 1: Offline eval — full-sweep on historical logs + synthetic low-resource augment (2 weeks)
Stage 2: Shadow canary — 0.5% global traffic, monitor MRR, latency, cost (3 days)
Stage 3: Regional canaries — enable for EU/APAC subsets with per-locale gates (1 week each)
Stage 4: Gradual expansion — double traffic every 24-48h if gates pass; automatic rollback on gate failure
Manual checkpoints: PM/ML lead sign-off before region promotion; Incident runbook prepared
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: High-quality scorer saturates GPU, causing elevated tail latency — Mitigation: autoscale hook + fallback to lightweight scorer when headroom < 12%
Risk: Silent quality regressions for niche locales — Mitigation: per-locale holdout tests and thresholded promotion; maintain historical baseline snapshots
Risk: Cost overruns if adoption is wider than expected — Mitigation: rollout cost throttle and quarterly budget alerts in Console
Risk: Model drift after promotion — Mitigation: daily eval jobs and rollback automation on sustained metric drift
